summary: # Marvelous Designer Three-Minute Classroom ## Why is My File Corrupted and Won’t Open? How to Save Files Correctly? ### Introduction In this video, we discuss common issues related to file corruption in Marvelous Designer and how to save files correctly to avoid these problems. ### Reasons for File Corruption After saving a project, you may encounter a situation where the document cannot be opened again, and various prompt frames are removed. There are several reasons for this issue, primarily related to the system font or the size of the document. ### Installation Path Considerations When installing Marvelous Designer, it is crucial to ensure that there are no special fonts or non-English words in the installation path. - **Special Fonts**: Avoid using special fonts such as "Signal," "Add," etc. - **Non-English Characters**: Refrain from using characters from languages such as Chinese, Japanese, or Korean. ### File Saving Guidelines The same considerations apply when storing project files or exporting files. Ensure that the path and file name adhere to the following recommendations: - Use paths such as "This Computer" or "Local Disk," which will not be affected by the aforementioned rules. - It is recommended to use Arabic numerals, English letters, and lowercase characters for file names. ### Internal Function Usage When utilizing the internal functions of Marvelous Designer, please ensure that the file path or name complies with the rules mentioned above. While using special fonts or non-English words may not always cause problems, avoiding them can help prevent unnecessary complications. ### Version Compatibility It is important to note that files created in a new version of Marvelous Designer may not be opened in an older version. However, files from an older version can typically be opened in the new version of the software. ### File Size Limitations If the entire project file exceeds 2GB, it may not be stored properly or could become damaged. For example, a project with minimal clothing (only 3mm) and a total of 1,500 animated frames could easily surpass this size limit. - **Display Statistics**: By enabling the display statistics function in the 3D window, you can view data such as the number of faces, points, and other metrics. ### Saving Project Files Let's test saving a project file. After navigating to the folder to check the file storage situation, you may notice that the size of the saved file has only increased to slightly over 200KB, indicating that the storage has failed. For animated files exceeding 2GB, it is advisable to save the project in separate sections from the beginning. For instance, if you recorded about 700 frames, save the project file after this recording. After saving, the number of frames should remain at the last recorded frame, and you can then delete the previously recorded animation. 1. Continue recording from the last frame. 2. Save this new animation as a new project file. By saving in sections, you should find that both project files are successfully saved and accessible. ### Exporting to Alembic Format When the project size exceeds 2GB, it can be exported to Alembic format (ABC). However, modifying the file after export can be challenging, so direct export is not recommended. If you are uncertain about the size of the entire project file, you can first export the ABC file to check its size. ### Conclusion This concludes the discussion on file corruption issues and saving methods in Marvelous Designer. If you have any questions, feel free to send a private message or leave a comment. See you in the next video! Bye bye.
